facts.fact: Disney's OTT service Disney+ launched in 2019, according to the article.
facts.quote: Disney’s OTT service called Disney+ launched in 2019.

facts.fact: NBC Universal launched its OTT service Peacock in 2020, according to the article.
facts.quote: NBC Universal launched its own OTT service–Peacock–in 2020.

facts.fact: According to eMarketer (a third-party source), more than one-third of US households will have cut the cord by 2024.
facts.quote: According to eMarketer, [more than one-third](https://content-na1.emarketer.com/pay-tv-suffers-historic-cord-cutting) of US households will have cut the cord by 2024.

facts.fact: Coinbase's 2022 Super Bowl ad was a 60-second spot, and after scanning its QR code users were offered $15 in free Bitcoin for opening a Coinbase account.
facts.quote: The company’s 60-second spot during America’s most-watched sporting event consisted of a QR code bouncing around the screen

facts.fact: According to TechCrunch (a third-party source), Coinbase's Super Bowl ad boosted app downloads by 309% immediately after airing and by an additional 289% the next day.
facts.quote: The ad skyrocketed [app downloads by 309%](https://techcrunch.com/2022/02/17/super-bowl-ads-boosted-crypto-app-downloads-by-279-led-by-coinbase/) immediately after the airing of the ad, and an additional 289% the next day.

facts.fact: CTV is defined as any TV capable of streaming digital video, including smart TVs and TVs connected to a device such as Roku or Chromecast.
facts.quote: The term connected TV (CTV) describes any TV capable of streaming digital video.

facts.fact: The page describes OTT as the content and CTV as the viewing method.
facts.quote: Think of OTT as the content and CTV as the viewing method.

facts.fact: The page defines OTT as the delivery of TV content through the internet instead of the standard, closed TV system.
facts.quote: OTT is the term that describes the delivery of TV content through the internet instead of the standard, closed TV system.

facts.fact: The page gives Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon Prime as examples of video-on-demand (VOD) apps that deliver OTT programming.
facts.quote: OTT is the programming you stream via video-on-demand (VOD) apps like Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon Prime.

facts.fact: The page gives Roku, Amazon FireStick, Google Chromecast, and smart TVs as examples of devices used to watch CTV programming.
facts.quote: Connected TV, or CTV, is the device you use to watch that programming like Roku, Amazon FireStick, Google Chromecast, or a smart TV.
